title: Group Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, Employees & Contractors
tiers.description: The IAG Group, IAG Board, Subsidiary Non-Executive Directors, Employees and Contractors, at all times including during leave or a career break. Subject only to the Inside Information prohibition and the front page test; no Trading Window, consent, short-term trading or margin lending restriction applies to this tier unless the person is also a Specified Person.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: Persons likely to come into contact with or have access to key financial, operational or strategic price-sensitive information: Non-Executive Directors of a Specified Board (IAG, Insurance Australia Limited, IAG New Zealand Limited, Insurance Manufacturers of Australia), the GCEO, GLT members, all direct reports to the GLT, and Company Secretaries of a Specified Board, plus other senior management roles the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary determines (reviewed every 6 months). Subject to Trading Windows, prior consent, the three-month short-term trading ban and the margin lending and collateral prohibition.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors of a Specified Board
tiers.description: A sub-set of Specified Persons distinguished only for the consent route and for post-trade obligations: consent from a more senior approver, plus a confirmation of trade to the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day so an ASX Appendix 3Y can be lodged within 5 business days.

tiers.name: IAG Board Chair
tiers.description: The IAG Board Chair, who approves out-of-window Exceptional Circumstances requests and in-window trading by other Non-Executive Directors, the GCEO and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary; the Chair's own requests go to the IAG Board Audit Committee Chair.

tiers.name: Closely Related Parties
tiers.description: Closely Related Party as defined in section 9 of the Corporations Act (spouse, dependants, certain other family members, companies and trusts controlled by the person). The Policy applies directly to them, and Specified Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure their compliance.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding IAG Securities.

windows.start_anchor: one ASX Trading Day after the half year results announcement
windows.end_anchor: typically 20 business days later, as notified by e-mail

windows.start_anchor: one ASX Trading Day after the final results announcement
windows.end_anchor: typically 20 business days later, as notified by e-mail

windows.start_anchor: one ASX Trading Day after the annual general meeting
windows.end_anchor: typically 20 business days later, as notified by e-mail

windows.start_anchor: additional Trading Windows designated by the Board at its discretion (e.g. following the issue of a prospectus or in a period of enhanced disclosure)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The IAG Board may vary, suspend or terminate Trading Windows arrangements, conditionally or unconditionally, at any time; Specified Persons are notified of windows by e-mail and must not assume a window is open in the absence of notification. The Board approves the opening of Trading Windows. Separately, approvers may refuse consent or impose conditions at any time without giving reasons, and a refusal must be kept confidential.

rules.section: 9-10, 14; Definitions (Securities, Dealing in/Trading in IAG Securities)
rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule. Securities expressly include financial products such as warrants, options, contracts for difference and other derivatives relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, IAG securities, whether or not created by IAG or a third party, so there is no venue or issuer limit. Applying for, acquiring or disposing of such a product, or entering into an agreement to do so, is a Dealing and needs a Trading Consent Request approved in a Trading Window, no Inside Information, and satisfaction of the front page test.
rules.evidence: financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by IAG Group or third parties.

rules.detail: For those who are not Specified Persons the only constraints on dealing in an IAG derivative are the Inside Information prohibition and the front page test; there is no Trading Window, consent or record-keeping requirement, and the margin lending prohibition in clause 34 does not reach them.
rules.evidence: This Policy prohibits you and your Closely Related Parties from Dealing in IAG Securities where you or they are in possession of Inside Information.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on hedging plan securities before vesting; it applies to any participant in an IAG employee, executive or director equity plan, not only Specified Persons, and extends to Closely Related Parties of Specified Persons. Hedging is defined broadly as any arrangement operating to limit economic risk associated with holding IAG Securities, so a purchased put over unvested rights is caught. No approval route exists.
rules.evidence: IAG Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG by any participant must never be hedged prior to vesting. This requirement also extends to Closely Related Parties of Specified Persons.

rules.detail: Vested shares that remain subject to a holding lock or a restriction on dealing under an IAG plan may never be hedged. This is a separate, absolute prohibition from the pre-vesting ban and again has no consent or exception route, so disposal restriction periods must have fully expired before any collar is placed over plan shares.
rules.evidence: IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is confined to plan securities that are unvested or under a holding lock, so hedging fully vested unrestricted shares (or shares acquired on market) is not banned. It is, however, a Dealing in Securities because instruments that operate to limit economic risk are themselves Securities, so it needs prior consent, a Trading Window, no Inside Information and satisfaction of the front page test, and any funding leg secured on the shares would separately breach clause 34.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding IAG Securities.

rules.detail: For a plan participant who is not a Specified Person, hedging vested, unlocked IAG securities is not prohibited and no consent or window applies; only the Inside Information prohibition and the front page test bite.
rules.evidence: IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named, but any monetisation that uses IAG Securities as collateral, including a loan secured on collared shares, is caught by the blanket prohibition on using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction. A monetisation with no collateral element (for example a cash-settled hedge over vested unrestricted shares with an unsecured loan) is only a Dealing requiring consent in a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and is not listed in the Dealing definition; only the Inside Information prohibition, the front page test and, for Specified Persons, the window, consent and three-month short-term trading rules would apply to any sale.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the Dealing definition (apply for, acquire or dispose of, or agree to do so). Depending on structure it could be characterised as a disposal, and a lend that secures a financing would be caught by the clause 34 collateral prohibition, but the Policy is silent.

Contracts for difference are expressly named as a category of Securities rather than in a prohibition, so dealing in one is a Dealing requiring consent within a Trading Window. In practice the three-month short-term trading ban in clause 30 and the front page test would defeat most CFD positions.
rules.evidence: financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities

rules.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities, and transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account, are both expressly prohibited for Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties. This prohibition was added by the 30 November 2023 amendment. There is no vesting-state carve-out, no grandfathering language for pre-existing arrangements, and no approval or exemption route.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by: a. entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities; or b. transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Clause 34 is located in the 'Other Restrictions' section that applies to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties only; the Policy imposes no margin lending restriction on other Directors, Employees or Contractors.

Granting security is not itself within the Dealing definition, but clause 34 prohibits the use of IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, which captures a mortgage, charge, pledge or security interest over IAG shares given to any financier, not just a margin lender. The two limbs that follow are expressly non-exhaustive examples.
rules.evidence: must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by:

rules.detail: No encumbrance restriction applies to Directors, Employees or Contractors who are not Specified Persons, and granting security is not a Dealing under the definition.

The prohibition is drafted at the level of collateral in 'any financial transaction', so it is broader than margin lending and covers a bank loan secured on collared shares, a limited recourse loan, a securities-backed lending facility and a prepaid forward supported by a share pledge. No approver may consent to it; the Exceptional Circumstances route in clauses 19 to 23 relieves only the Trading Window requirement, not clause 34.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction

rules.detail: The Policy says nothing about secured financing by Directors, Employees or Contractors who are not Specified Persons.

A flat three-month gap is required between a purchase and a sale of any IAG Securities by a Specified Person or their Closely Related Party. No carve-outs are stated for plan vesting, DRP acquisitions or exercise of rights, although the clause 27 exclusions take those dealings outside the Policy generally. Because derivatives are Securities, a collar with a tenor or unwind inside three months of any acquisition is exposed to this ban.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.

rules.detail: The no-speculative-trading rule is confined to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties.

Consents to trade ... will be effective for 5 business days (but no later than the last day of the Trading Window), unless a different timeframe is specified in the consent provided.

clearance.approver: GCEO and Group General Counsel & Company Secretary under the clause 14 table; the roles table at clause 36 instead assigns approval of trading by other Non-Executive Directors, the GCEO and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary to the IAG Board Chair
clearance.post_trade_to: Group Company Secretary (confirmation of trade so an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 1 business day after execution of the trade
clearance.evidence: IAG Directors who undertake a Dealing in IAG Securities following consent must provide the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day of the execution of the trade a confirmation of trade so that an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days after the change has occurred.

clearance.post_trade_to: Group Company Secretary (confirmation of trade for the ASX Appendix 3Y)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 1 business day after execution of the trade
clearance.evidence: IAG Board Chair | IAG Board Audit Committee Chair

Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties may only deal in IAG Securities during a Trading Window, and only if they are not in possession of Inside Information and the trade would satisfy the front page test.

short_term.basis: three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities
short_term.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.

The IAG Board Chair ... may consent to a Specified Person Dealing in IAG Securities outside a Trading Window if: a. in the opinion of the IAG Board Chair, Exceptional Circumstances have been evidenced, and the proposed trade in IAG Securities is the most reasonable course of action available in the circumstances

exceptions.evidence: Compulsion by court order or court enforceable undertaking (for example, a bona fide family settlement);
Some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to transfer or accept transfer of Securities; or d. Such other circumstance determined by the Chair.

indirect or incidental Trading in IAG Securities that occurs as a consequence of a Specified Person dealing in units or shares of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund, or similar investment vehicle managed by a third party that happens to hold IAG Securities as part of its portfolio and where the Specified Person is not in a position to influence the portfolio investments;

exceptions.evidence: transfers of IAG Securities between a Specified Person and their Closely Related Party in respect of which consent has been provided by an Approver or by a Specified Person to his or her self-managed superannuation fund (i.e. where there is equal information between that Specified Person and the trustee of the fund).

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Dealings involving conditional orders (for example a specified minimum sell or maximum purchase price, or a stop-loss instruction) must be both placed and executed during a Trading Window; ordinary on-market orders at market price may be placed until market close on the last day of a Trading Window.
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Mandatory Holdings is defined as the minimum holding of IAG ordinary shares required to be attained by IAG Directors and by the GCEO and GLT in accordance with IAG's Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy, which is listed as a related document. The definition is not tied to any operative clause of this Policy, and the Policy is silent on whether hedged or encumbered shares count toward the requirement.

external_documents: Terms and conditions of employment contracts and Non-Executive Directors' letters of appointment
Exceptional Circumstances Trading Consent Request form
Rules of IAG employee, executive and director equity plans (holding locks and dealing restrictions)
IAG Policy intranet page list of Specified Persons
exemption_authority: The IAG Board Chair (the IAG Board Audit Committee Chair where the request is from the Chair) may consent to a Specified Person Dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances, on evidence, if the trade is the most reasonable course of action available and the person holds no Inside Information and satisfies the front page test; the trade must be completed within 5 business days unless otherwise specified. That relief goes only to the Trading Window requirement. No officer has power to waive the hedging prohibitions in clauses 32 and 33, the margin lending and collateral prohibition in clause 34 or the three-month short-term trading ban in clause 30; only the IAG Board can change the Policy itself (the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary may make minor administrative changes and approve changes to the Specified Persons list).
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand: IAG is listed on the NZX and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 insider trading regime applies alongside the Australian Corporations Act 2001
Australia: ASX Listing Rule 12.10 and Guidance Note 27; Appendix 3Y director notifications

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not use IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including by: a. entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of IAG Securities; or b. transferring IAG Securities into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is squarely prohibited for every Specified Person and their Closely Related Parties, with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, so the structure cannot be offered to this population as designed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition is on collateral in 'any financial transaction'; the margin lending and margin account limbs are introduced by 'including by', so they are examples rather than the limit.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Recharacterising the facility as a securities-backed loan, a limited recourse loan or a pledged prepaid forward does not escape clause 34.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means ... financial products (such as warrants, options, performance rights, contracts for difference and other derivatives) relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by IAG Group or third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs written by a bank are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll, exercise, unwind and settlement are each separate Dealings requiring their own consent within a Trading Window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IAG Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by IAG by any participant must never be hedged prior to vesting ... IAG securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an unfunded collar can only be placed over plan shares that have vested and are free of any holding lock, and the ban reaches Closely Related Parties so a family trust holding cannot be used.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings involving conditional orders must be placed and executed during a Trading Window (e.g., a specified, minimum sell or maximum purchase price or a stop-loss instruction).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any price-triggered feature of a collar - a knock-in or knock-out barrier, automatic unwind or stop-loss - must both trigger and complete inside a Trading Window, which is impractical for a multi-year structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where consent is required for a trade under this Policy, consent will not be granted where the approver does not consider that the trade would satisfy the front page test. This decision of the approver is final.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over an executive's shareholding is precisely the kind of trade that may be judged to look inappropriate on the front page, and the approver's refusal is final, unreasoned and confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent may be withdrawn if new information is revealed or there is a change in circumstances, and that decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the Specified Person seeking consent and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on consent surviving to signing or settlement, and the executive cannot explain a withdrawal to the counterparty because it must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consents to trade ... will be effective for 5 business days (but no later than the last day of the Trading Window), unless a different timeframe is specified in the consent provided.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the derivative legs must complete within 5 business days and before the window closes, so documentation must be fully negotiated before consent is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties must not deal in IAG Securities on a short-term trading basis, being a period of three months between purchase and sale of any IAG Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because derivatives are Securities with no stated carve-outs, a collar's purchased put and written call and any unwind must be spaced more than three months from related purchases and sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specified Persons must not assume that a Trading Window is open in the absence of notification, as the IAG Board may vary, suspend or terminate (conditionally or unconditionally) Trading Windows arrangements at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution and unwind dates cannot be committed in advance, since the Board can close a window at any time and the only relief is a discretionary Exceptional Circumstances consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clause 14's table routes consent requests from Non-Executive Directors of a Specified Board (excluding the IAG Board Chair) to the 'GCEO and Group General Counsel & Company Secretary', while the clause 36 roles table gives the IAG Board Chair responsibility to approve trading by other Non-Executive Directors, the GCEO and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a director-level collar the correct approver is ambiguous on the face of the Policy, so the bank should require evidence of consent from both the Chair and the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls, lender enforcement and pre-existing financing arrangements; there is no grandfathering wording accompanying the clause 34 prohibition added in the 30 November 2023 amendment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out permitting a secured lender to sell during a closed period, and no stated transition for legacy secured facilities, so any existing arrangement is exposed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Mandatory Holdings means the minimum holding of IAG ordinary shares required to be attained by IAG Directors and by the GCEO and GLT, in accordance with IAG's Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The separate Mandatory Shareholding Requirement Policy may require an unhedged minimum holding and must be diligenced, as this Policy neither operationalises nor excludes hedged shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IAG Directors who undertake a Dealing in IAG Securities following consent must provide the Group Company Secretary within 1 business day of the execution of the trade a confirmation of trade so that an ASX Appendix 3Y can be completed and lodged with the ASX within 5 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's collar would become publicly disclosed on an Appendix 3Y within days of execution, which feeds back into the front page test at the consent stage.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for IAG Specified Persons, the population that includes the directors and executives a bank would target. Clause 34, added by the 30 November 2023 amendment, prohibits Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties from using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, with margin lending and transfers into a margin account given only as examples, and no approver has power to waive it. The derivative legs alone are also constrained: instruments that limit economic risk are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trading Consent Request approved by the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary (or, for Non-Executive Directors, the more senior approver route), inside one of the three roughly 20 business day Trading Windows, valid for only 5 business days, subject to the front page test whose refusal is final and confidential, and subject to the three-month short-term trading ban. Plan shares can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, so only fully vested unrestricted shares are candidates, and any price-triggered or conditional feature must be both placed and executed within a window. A collar could in principle be offered on an unsecured basis over vested unrestricted shares, and Directors, Employees and Contractors who are not Specified Persons are not caught by clauses 30 or 34 at all, but for the target population the funded structure is barred.
